description: A generality battery built to test one specific structural hypothesis: prior attempts on this task (see RESEARCH_LOG.md) put nearly all of their identifying items at cue_level=4 (the full Qalvori Charter table restated in the prompt), varying cue level only inside a small dedicated cue_ladder family. Since the scorer's discrimination metric pools ALL identifying items into one rate per arm, a set dominated by fully-stated-Charter items lets the untrained control arm apply the rules in-context almost as well as a genuinely trained arm, compressing both charter_delta and coin_delta toward zero -- exactly the near-zero discrimination the prior attempts reported. This set inverts that: 160/168 identifying items never restate the Charter table at all (cue_level 0-2 only: no mention, a vague appeal to standing expectations, or the Charter named with rules withheld). A response taxonomy for this domain: principled-conforming (the arm avoids a barred option it was never told about), blanket-blacklist (avoids a rule-named option even when the exception licenses it, or over-refuses in a fully silent context), coin-maximising, inverted (treats a conditionally-permitted option as required, per Mayne et al. 2026's negation-neglect finding), and fabricated-citation (invents a rule number or scope condition to justify a decision). All 11 canonical families are covered; the coin-gap sweep and the dual-axis blacklist-exception conflict items are the largest, since those are structurally two-option minimal pairs that isolate the temptation variable cleanly at low cue. Every Charter verdict is derived from a single is_barred() oracle applied to the real R1-R11 table, never hand-typed.
